paragraphs.title: The Beginning of Joash's Reign and the Renewal of the Temple

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.”
easy.q: How old was Joash when he began to reign?

easy.explanation: Joash did what was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
easy.q: Who influenced Joash to do what was right in the sight of the LORD?

answers: To restore and strengthen the Temple
easy.explanation: Joash was minded to repair the house of the LORD, and the workmen restored and strengthened it.
easy.q: Why did Joash want to repair the house of the LORD?

answers: It had been broken up and its dedicated things given to Baalim
The king wanted to move into it
There was not enough room for the people
medium.explanation: The sons of Athaliah had broken up the house of God and given its dedicated things to Baalim.
medium.q: Why did the house of God need to be repaired?

answers: By placing a chest at the gate of the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: A chest was made and set outside the gate of the house of the LORD for the collection.
medium.q: How was money collected for repairing the house of the LORD?

medium.explanation: The collection was money brought by Israel according to the commandment given through Moses.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the collection” refer to?

answers: The gifts were gathered without order
challenge.explanation: The king’s scribe and the high priest’s officer emptied the chest and returned it to its place day by day.
challenge.q: What does the daily emptying of the chest show about the handling of the money?

answers: It was divided among the princes
It was sent to the king of Damascus
It was used to make vessels for the house of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The rest of the money was used to make vessels for service and worship in the house of the LORD.
challenge.q: What was done with the money left after the repairs were completed?

answers: The Temple was repaired, vessels were made, and burnt offerings continued
The repairs ended worship at the Temple
The money was used only for the king’s needs
challenge.explanation: After the repairs, vessels were made, and burnt offerings were offered continually all the days of Jehoiada.
challenge.q: How were the repair of the building and the worship of God connected?

easy.explanation: The KJV says Jehoiada was one hundred and thirty years old when he died.
easy.q: How old was Jehoiada when he died?

answers: In the city of David among the kings
easy.explanation: They buried Jehoiada in the city of David among the kings.
Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada, was stoned in the court of the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Who was killed after warning the people?

answers: He strengthened the worship of the LORD
He listened to Judah’s princes and abandoned the worship of the LORD
medium.explanation: After Jehoiada’s death, the princes came to the king, and he hearkened unto them; the people then left the house of the LORD.
medium.q: What changed in Joash’s behavior after Jehoiada died?

answers: To bring them again unto the LORD
medium.explanation: The prophets were sent to bring the people again unto the LORD, but they would not give ear.
medium.q: Why did the LORD send prophets to the people?

answers: Anger or judgment came upon Judah
medium.explanation: The wrath came because Judah and Jerusalem had forsaken the LORD and served groves and idols.
medium.q: What does “wrath came upon Judah” mean in this context?

answers: Jehoiada received honor, while Joash was denied burial in the kings’ sepulchres
challenge.explanation: Jehoiada was buried among the kings because he had done good, but Joash was not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown by Jehoiada’s burial and Joash’s burial?

answers: They were transgressing the LORD’s commandments and would not prosper
challenge.explanation: Zechariah asked, “Why transgress ye the commandments of the LORD, that ye cannot prosper?”
challenge.q: What was the substance of Zechariah’s warning?

answers: Forsaking the LORD would result in the LORD forsaking them
Repairing the Temple would cause war
Listening to a prophet would cause captivity
challenge.explanation: Zechariah declared, “because ye have forsaken the LORD, he hath also forsaken you.”
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect statement appears in Zechariah’s words?

paragraphs.title: The Aramean Invasion and Joash's Punishment

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “the host of Syria came up against him.”
easy.q: What army came against Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: They restored Joash to the throne
They destroyed them and carried away the spoil
easy.explanation: The Syrians destroyed the princes and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.
easy.q: What did the Syrians do to Judah and its princes?

easy.explanation: Joash’s own servants conspired against him and slew him on his bed.
easy.q: Who killed Joash after the Syrians withdrew?

answers: It was small, yet defeated a very great host
medium.explanation: The Syrian army came with a small company of men, but the LORD delivered a very great host into their hand.
medium.q: How is the size of the Syrian army contrasted with its victory?

answers: Judah had forsaken the LORD God of their fathers
medium.explanation: The passage says the LORD delivered Judah into their hand because they had forsaken him.
medium.q: Why did the Syrians defeat Judah, according to the passage?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the serious suffering Joash endured after the Syrians departed.
medium.q: What does “great diseases” mean in the description of Joash’s condition?

answers: As judgment connected with forsaking the LORD
As an event without a cause
As a reward for repairing the Temple
challenge.explanation: The text directly connects the Syrian victory with Judah’s forsaking of the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the chapter present the Syrian invasion morally?

answers: Joash’s servants killed him for the blood of Jehoiada’s sons
challenge.explanation: Joash’s servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada, including Zechariah.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Zechariah’s death and Joash’s death?

answers: He was not descended from David
He was denied the honorable burial given to worthy kings
challenge.explanation: The burial distinction shows that Joash did not receive the same honor as the kings buried in the royal sepulchres.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Joash being buried in the city of David but not in the kings’ sepulchres?

paragraphs.title: The Conspirators and the Continuation of the Davidic Dynasty

answers: Amaziah and the king of Damascus
easy.explanation: The conspirators were Zabad the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith.
easy.q: Who were the two conspirators against Joash?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.”
Amaziah, Joash’s son, became king after him.
easy.q: What happened to the monarchy after Joash died?

answers: They were members of the king’s family
The deed is attributed to specific individuals
medium.explanation: The passage identifies the conspirators by name, parentage, and maternal background.
medium.q: What does the naming of the conspirators and their mothers’ peoples emphasize?

answers: It ended the house of David
It led to the reign of Joash’s son
medium.explanation: Although Joash was killed, Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.
medium.q: How did the conspirators’ action affect the government of Judah?

medium.explanation: Amaziah reigned in Joash’s stead, meaning he took his place as king.

answers: The conspirators killed Joash, but his son continued to reign
The conspirators transferred the throne to Syria
challenge.explanation: Joash died, but the Davidic monarchy continued through Amaziah his son.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between attacking Joash and attacking the dynasty?

answers: He began by repairing the Temple but ended in apostasy, defeat, and death
He began with war and ended by building the Temple
challenge.explanation: Joash first repaired the house of the LORD, but later forsook the LORD, permitted Zechariah’s death, suffered defeat, and was killed.
challenge.q: How does the chapter present the results of Joash’s actions throughout his life?

answers: Amaziah reigned after Joash, although Joash was not buried in the kings’ sepulchres
Joash was buried with all the kings
Syria placed Amaziah on the throne
challenge.explanation: Joash received an unusual burial, yet his son Amaziah continued the royal line.
challenge.q: Which detail most clearly supports the distinction between Joash and the continuation of David’s house?
